title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Shelby Cobra

scenes.text: The Shelby Cobra, one of the most famous American cars ever made, started as a British car with no engine, shipped by air to California. And its most famous version, the four hundred twenty-seven, had a rule it never met. The rules said a hundred had to be built. Wikipedia says only fifty-six were. These are the two things about the Shelby Cobra that most people do not know.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE SHELBY COBRA

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The first Cobra was finished in under eight hours. And the car that people call the fastest Cobra of all was not allowed to race in the year it was built. One of the things we will show you also explains why a single Cobra later sold for thirteen point seven five million dollars. Stay to the end.
scenes.caption: EIGHT HOURS · 56 OF 100 · $13.75 MILLION

scenes.text: Every number in this video comes from published sources, listed in the description. Where sources disagree, we will tell you. Where we do the maths ourselves, we will say so.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: Start with the AC Ace. Wikipedia says AC Cars of Thames Ditton, England, had built the Ace roadster since nineteen fifty-three, designed by John Tojeiro. It used a steel ladder chassis with three-inch main rails, and a straight six engine. It was a pretty, light British sports car. Nothing about it suggested a muscle car.
scenes.caption: THE AC ACE: A BRITISH ROADSTER FROM 1953
scenes.chapter: Thing one: a car with no engine

scenes.text: Then, in September nineteen sixty-one, according to the Cobra page, Ford gave Carroll Shelby two new two hundred twenty-one cubic inch small-block V eights, and one went to AC in England. The AC Ace page adds that Shelby had proposed fitting a Ford V eight to the Ace chassis in nineteen sixty-one. That was the idea. The question was whether it would work.
scenes.caption: SEPTEMBER 1961: FORD GIVES SHELBY TWO V8s

scenes.text: In January nineteen sixty-two, AC completed the prototype at Thames Ditton. It was called C S X two thousand. Wikipedia says it was air-freighted to Shelby in Los Angeles on the second of February nineteen sixty-two. By our own arithmetic, the engine was given to AC in September, and the car arrived in California in February, about five months later.
scenes.caption: 2 FEBRUARY 1962: CSX2000 ARRIVES IN LOS ANGELES

scenes.text: And now the first surprise. Wikipedia says Shelby's team installed the engine and transmission in C S X two thousand in under eight hours, at Dean Moon's shop in Santa Fe Springs, California. Jalopnik adds that the car arrived in the United States without an engine, and that Shelby and Moon fitted a two hundred sixty cubic inch V eight and a Ford four-speed gearbox.
scenes.caption: ENGINE AND GEARBOX FITTED IN UNDER EIGHT HOURS

scenes.text: Dean Moon, Jalopnik says, tested the car on an improvised road course between oil derricks, and its durability convinced them it was good. The Ford engine in the prototype was larger than the original: Wikipedia says the displacement grew to four point three litres, two hundred sixty cubic inches. Another reference on that page lists four point two. So the sources differ slightly on the engine size.
scenes.caption: TESTED ON A ROAD COURSE BETWEEN OIL DERRICKS

scenes.text: The result was fast. EVO reports that Road and Track tested the car in nineteen sixty-two and timed zero to sixty miles per hour at four point two seconds, with a top speed of a hundred fifty-three. EVO says that beat the hundred fifty miles per hour of the Series One Jaguar E-Type. By our arithmetic, the Cobra was three miles per hour quicker at the top end.
scenes.caption: ROAD & TRACK 1962: 0–60 IN 4.2 S · 153 MPH

scenes.text: The original budget was small. Jalopnik says Shelby built the car on a small budget, then got funding from Ford to build the first group of Cobras. Carroll Shelby's own page says production began in March nineteen sixty-two, with seventy-five cars sold by the end of that year, and a hundred built by April nineteen sixty-three.
scenes.caption: 75 SOLD IN 1962 · 100 BUILT BY APRIL 1963

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, a hundred cars in about thirteen months is less than eight cars a month. That is a tiny operation next to Detroit. Yet the car in question went on to win championships and to be copied around the world. It began as one prototype, an engine on a plane, and an eight-hour installation. The speed of it all is part of the story.
scenes.caption: <8 CARS A MONTH (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The prototype still exists. EVO says that C S X two thousand was in the same ownership for over fifty years, never leaving Shelby's care. It retains its early AC shell, since later Cobras had wider bodywork to fit larger tyres. It appeared at Pebble Beach in two thousand twelve and was displayed at the Shelby Heritage Center in Las Vegas.
scenes.caption: THE PROTOTYPE KEPT ITS EARLY AC BODY

scenes.text: In August two thousand sixteen, at R M Sotheby's Monterey sale, it sold for thirteen point seven five million dollars, about fifteen minutes of bidding, according to EVO. Jalopnik called it a record for an American car at auction. The previous record, it says, was a nineteen sixty-eight Ford G T forty that sold in two thousand twelve for eleven million dollars.
scenes.caption: AUGUST 2016: $13.75 MILLION · AMERICAN AUCTION RECORD

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, thirteen point seven five million is twenty-five percent more than the eleven million of the G T forty. And it is more than nine times the one and a half million that the Du Pont Registry lists for an original four hundred twenty-seven. The prototype was the car that began everything, and the market valued it accordingly.
scenes.caption: +25% OVER THE PREVIOUS RECORD (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Early production had its own quirks. Wikipedia says the first seventy-five Mark One cars, including the prototype, used the two hundred sixty cubic inch engine, and the remaining fifty-one used the two hundred eighty-nine. Shelby later offered upgrades to the larger engine, so cars with the original two hundred sixty are rare today. That adds up, by our arithmetic, to one hundred twenty-six Mark One cars.
scenes.caption: 75 WITH THE 260 · 51 WITH THE 289 (126 MK I)

scenes.text: There were cost changes too. The page says the inboard brakes moved outboard to cut cost, and the fuel filler moved from the fender to the boot. These are small changes, but they show a car being turned from a prototype into something that could be sold. The AC Ace page adds that the Cobra inherited the lower bonnet and smaller grille developed for the Ace two point six.
scenes.caption: COST CUTS: OUTBOARD BRAKES, FUEL FILLER IN THE BOOT

scenes.text: That last point is a correction to the legend. Shelby is often credited with the Cobra's lower nose, the Ace page says, but that shape was developed for the Ace two point six, a car with a Ford Zephyr six-cylinder engine. Only thirty-seven of those Ruddspeed cars were made. The Cobra's looks were, in part, inherited from an even rarer British car.
scenes.caption: THE LOW NOSE CAME FROM THE ACE 2.6 (ONLY 37 BUILT)

scenes.text: And the Ace's life ended soon after. The page says Ace production ended one year after the Cobra debuted. In other words, the car that gave Shelby his platform disappeared almost as soon as the Cobra arrived. By our reading, the Cobra replaced the Ace in the factory as well as in the public mind, and we compare the two directly in another video of this series.
scenes.caption: ACE PRODUCTION ENDED A YEAR AFTER THE COBRA DEBUTED

scenes.text: Now the second surprise. The most famous Cobra is the four hundred twenty-seven. Wikipedia describes the third generation, the Mark Three, with a chassis of four-inch tubes and coil springs all round. It says the chassis was designed together with Ford in Detroit. The standard engine was the seven litre, four hundred twenty-seven cubic inch F E V eight.
scenes.caption: THE MARK III: 427 CUBIC INCHES, COIL SPRINGS
scenes.chapter: Thing two: the car that was not allowed to race

scenes.text: It was rated at four hundred twenty-five horsepower with a seven hundred eighty C F M Holley carburettor. Top speed, according to Wikipedia, was a hundred sixty-four miles per hour as standard, and a hundred eighty-five for the S slash C, tuned to four hundred eighty-five horsepower. Those are numbers from the nineteen sixties. They would still impress today.
scenes.caption: 425 HP · 164 MPH · S/C: 485 HP · 185 MPH

scenes.text: Here is the surprise. Wikipedia says production began on the first of January nineteen sixty-five. But only fifty-six of the hundred required cars were built. Of those, thirty-one unsold competition cars were detuned and fitted with windscreens for street use. And the page says the Mark Three was not homologated for the nineteen sixty-five racing season, and was not raced by the Shelby team.
scenes.caption: ONLY 56 OF THE 100 REQUIRED CARS BUILT

scenes.text: Let us be careful. The homologation rules required a number of cars to be built for a model to be allowed to compete. The page says a hundred were required, and that fifty-six were built. By our arithmetic, that is fifty-six percent of the requirement, forty-four cars short. It also gives a discrepancy: another section of the page says fifty-five were originally built.
scenes.caption: 56% OF THE REQUIREMENT (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SOURCE ALSO SAYS 55

scenes.text: The sources do not say what the exact rule was or who enforced it, so we will not guess. What they do say is that the car was not homologated for nineteen sixty-five and did not race for Shelby. The Cobra racing history was written by the smaller engined cars, such as the two hundred eighty-nine and the Daytona Coupe, not by the four hundred twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: THE 427 WASN'T THE RACING COBRA

scenes.text: The Daytona Coupe was the one that raced. Wikipedia says six Daytona Cobra Coupés were built for Le Mans, rated at three hundred eighty-five horsepower. Carroll Shelby's page says the Daytona Coupe won three G T class wins in nineteen sixty-four, including Le Mans and Goodwood, and the S C C A U S G T Championship.
scenes.caption: DAYTONA COUPE: 6 BUILT · CLASS WINS 1964

scenes.text: And in nineteen sixty-five, the same page says, the Cobra won the International Championship for G T Manufacturers. Jalopnik, by contrast, mentions the Cobra's nineteen sixty-five Le Mans in connection with the success of the two hundred eighty-nine Cobras. The sources describe the same achievements in slightly different words, and none gives us a full results table.
scenes.caption: 1965: INTERNATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP FOR GT MANUFACTURERS

scenes.text: Another detail from the Wikipedia page adds colour. Ken Miles raced a Ford F E powered Mark Two at Sebring and called it The Turd. It retired with an engine failure. At Nassau, a six point four litre, three hundred ninety cubic inch car led by the length of the straight after one lap, but retired with brake problems. The big engine was thrilling and difficult.
scenes.caption: KEN MILES CALLED HIS BIG-ENGINE COBRA "THE TURD"

scenes.text: If the four hundred twenty-seven did not race, why is it a legend? Because of the numbers. Du Pont Registry lists three hundred sixty horsepower and four hundred nineteen pound-feet of torque in its spec sheet, zero to sixty miles per hour in three point four seconds, and a quarter mile in twelve point two at a hundred eighteen. These differ from Wikipedia's four hundred twenty-five horsepower rating.
scenes.caption: DU PONT: 360 HP · 3.4 S TO 60 · 1/4 MILE 12.2 S
scenes.chapter: Why the 427 is still a legend

scenes.text: That is a discrepancy worth noting. Wikipedia lists four hundred twenty-five horsepower for the standard engine and four hundred eighty-five for the S slash C. Du Pont Registry's spec list says three hundred sixty. The numbers may refer to different ratings, such as net and gross, but neither source says so. We report both, and we do not claim which is right.
scenes.caption: SOURCES DISAGREE: 425 HP (WIKIPEDIA) VS 360 HP (DU PONT)

scenes.text: The weight is not in dispute. Du Pont Registry lists two thousand, three hundred fifty-five pounds, and another section says under twenty-four hundred. By our arithmetic, two thousand three hundred fifty-five pounds is about one thousand, sixty-eight kilograms. With four hundred twenty-five horsepower, that gives roughly one horsepower for every five and a half pounds, which is extraordinary even now.
scenes.caption: 2,355 LB ≈ 1,068 KG · ~1 HP PER 5.5 LB (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Du Pont Registry says the original release price was seven thousand, five hundred dollars, and notes that in nineteen sixty-six it was priced well above any other American car. An original four hundred twenty-seven now sells, it says, for upwards of a million dollars. A Hagerty price guide, dated April twenty twenty-five, lists a number three good condition S slash C at two point two five million.
scenes.caption: NEW: $7,500 · HAGERTY #3 GOOD (APR 2025): $2.25M

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, two million, two hundred fifty thousand dollars divided by seven thousand, five hundred is three hundred times the original price. Remember that the figures are not strictly comparable. One is a published new price, the other a guide value for a specific S slash C. But the size of the multiple tells you something about how the Cobra has aged.
scenes.caption: $2.25M ÷ $7,500 = 300× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Cobra story has stranger branches. Wikipedia lists the Dragon Snake, of which six two hundred eighty-nine cars and one four hundred twenty-seven were built at the factory. And the Super Snake, chassis C S X three zero one five, converted in nineteen sixty-six with twin Paxton superchargers. Shelby later used it personally.
scenes.caption: DRAGON SNAKE · SUPER SNAKE (TWIN PAXTON SUPERCHARGERS)

scenes.text: The Super Snake sold for five million dollars at Barrett-Jackson in January two thousand seven, the page says, which it converts to about seven point two seven million dollars in two thousand twenty-four. By our arithmetic, the Super Snake's price was about thirty-six percent of the prototype's thirteen point seven five million, which sold nine years later. Both are single cars, with single stories.
scenes.caption: SUPER SNAKE: $5M IN JAN 2007 (≈ $7.27M IN 2024 DOLLARS)

scenes.text: There were also competition specials. The Wikipedia page mentions a Slalom Special, chassis C S X twenty-five twenty-two, and a Slalom Snake, twenty-five thirty-seven, the only autocross examples. And a Le Mans coupé, chassis A ninety-eight, which qualified second in G T in nineteen sixty-four with an engine rated at three hundred fifty-five horsepower.
scenes.caption: SLALOM SPECIAL · SLALOM SNAKE · LE MANS COUPÉ A98

scenes.text: That Le Mans car had a rear differential ratio of two point eight eight, compared with three point oh seven for the Daytona, the page says. A taller ratio means a higher top speed at the cost of acceleration. Two cars from the same factory, tuned for different priorities, a small detail that shows the engineering was real, not only marketing.
scenes.caption: DIFF RATIO: 2.88 (A98) VS 3.07 (DAYTONA)

scenes.text: Now a warning, from the same page. The Cobra is among the most copied cars in history. Wikipedia describes AC building the coil-spring roadster with a two hundred eighty-nine until late nineteen sixty-nine, the AC four twenty-eight Frua on a stretched chassis until nineteen seventy-three, and in nineteen eighty-six Autokraft buying AC and building the Mark Four with a four point nine five litre V eight.
scenes.caption: AC CARS: 289 UNTIL 1969 · 428 FRUA UNTIL 1973 · MK IV FROM 1987
scenes.chapter: The Cobras that were never built by Shelby

scenes.text: The Mark Four had two hundred fifty horsepower, a top speed of a hundred thirty-four, zero to sixty-two in five point two seconds, and weighed two thousand, six hundred twenty pounds. The page says a total of four hundred eighty cars of all versions were built until nineteen ninety-six. Those cars are not the nineteen sixties originals, and the page treats them as separate series.
scenes.caption: MK IV: 250 HP · 134 MPH · 480 CARS OF ALL VERSIONS UNTIL 1996

scenes.text: Then there are the continuation cars, with C S X numbers from four thousand to nine thousand. The page lists the C S X four thousand series, a four hundred twenty-seven S slash C continuation built from McCluskey chassis, which took about twenty years, ending in two thousand nine. And a limited run of fifty in twenty fourteen for the four hundred twenty-seven's fiftieth anniversary.
scenes.caption: CSX4000 SERIES: ABOUT 20 YEARS · 2014: A RUN OF 50

scenes.text: Du Pont Registry notes that A C Cobra prices have stayed under seven figures, partly because of the continuation cars. That is an important point for anyone shopping. A car described as a Cobra might be an original, a continuation or a replica, and the difference is not small. Most continuation cars, the Wikipedia page says, are fibreglass, with some aluminium or carbon fibre.
scenes.caption: ORIGINAL, CONTINUATION OR REPLICA: A HUGE DIFFERENCE

scenes.text: The page also records a controversy. In nineteen ninety-three, the Los Angeles Times reported that Shelby had obtained forty-three duplicate titles for Cobras not in AC's records. Shelby said the chassis were built by McCluskey Limited in nineteen ninety-one to ninety-two, and claimed a rival was behind the report. We report both sides. We do not take a side, because the page does not settle it.
scenes.caption: 1993: 43 DUPLICATE TITLES REPORTED — SHELBY DISPUTED THE REPORT

scenes.text: Carroll Shelby's own page adds that the so-called completion Cobras were allegedly built from leftover parts, that Shelby skipped blocks of V I N numbers to meet homologation requirements, and that the cars were later relabelled continuation Cobras. Again it says allegedly. We pass it on as an allegation on a public page, not as a finding.
scenes.caption: "COMPLETION" COBRAS WERE LATER RELABELLED "CONTINUATION" (ALLEGED)

scenes.text: The Wikipedia page contains a detail that shows how the Cobra was made. The Mark Two, redesigned by Alan Turner, used a rack-and-pinion steering rack from the M G B and a column from the Volkswagen Beetle. Those were cheap, widely available parts, bolted into a car that would later be worth millions. That is the Cobra: parts-bin pragmatism and a huge engine.
scenes.caption: STEERING RACK FROM AN MGB · COLUMN FROM A VW BEETLE

scenes.text: About five hundred twenty-eight Mark Two cars were built from nineteen sixty-three to the summer of nineteen sixty-five, the page says, with the last U.S.-bound car built in November nineteen sixty-four. The page itself notes that the chassis numbers cover only sixty-two numbers, so the figure does not match the numbering. Wikipedia flags the inconsistency, and so do we.
scenes.caption: ~528 MK II BUILT — BUT THE NUMBERING DOESN'T MATCH

scenes.text: Du Pont Registry says Shelby American built nine hundred ninety-eight Cobras in total, and delivered six hundred fifty-five small-block cars with leaf springs. By our arithmetic, nine ninety-eight less six fifty-five is three hundred forty-three, which would be the number of other types. That includes the big-block cars. Wikipedia's Mark One total is one hundred twenty-six, which is a different count.
scenes.caption: 998 TOTAL · 655 SMALL-BLOCK LEAF-SPRING (DU PONT)

scenes.text: The Cobra, by Wikipedia's account, was a financial failure. Ford and Shelby ended imports from England in nineteen sixty-seven. The page says this plainly. So the car that is now worth millions did not make its makers rich. That is the third thing, a bonus for those who stayed to the end: the legend is much bigger than the profit ever was.
scenes.caption: A FINANCIAL FAILURE — AND A LEGEND

scenes.text: Put the two things together. A car born in an eight-hour installation, from a plane delivery and a borrowed engine. A car whose most famous version missed the production target of its own racing rules. Neither fact lowers the Cobra's reputation. Both show how loose and improvised the early years were, compared with the tightly managed supercars of today.
scenes.caption: IMPROVISED, FAST AND FAMOUS (OUR READING)

scenes.text: Compare it with the other cars of this series. The Mercedes-AMG One took five years and a lot of engineering to make a Formula One engine idle. The Lexus LFA took ten. The Cobra took a few months. Different eras, different rules, and different budgets. But a few months is the number that stays with us, and it is why the car has a legend.
scenes.caption: FEW MONTHS · 5 YEARS · 10 YEARS (OUR READING)

scenes.text: A last caution. We have not driven a Cobra. The sources differ on engine size, power rating, and production counts, and we told you where. Some prices are guides, not sales. Where we did arithmetic, we said so. If you own or have worked on a Cobra and know a verified detail we missed, tell us in the comments, with where it comes from.
scenes.caption: SOURCES DIFFER ON ENGINE SIZE, POWER AND COUNTS

scenes.text: Which of the two things surprised you more, the eight-hour build or the missing forty-four cars? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we compare the Cobra with the AC Ace, work out what a real one costs today, and tell the story of the man who built it. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
